verdict.line: You lose if you take extended trades or get all-in'd before level 6; you win any fight from 6 onward where you can hold Riposte for his E or R.

brief.thesis: Fiora's W (Riposte) hard-counters the two abilities that make Darius dangerous — E (Apprehend) engage and R (Noxian Guillotine) execute — so once you hit level 6 a well-timed parry removes his entire kill threat. Before that, his passive Hemorrhage bleed stacks and empowered W (Crippling Strike) autos let him win extended trades and threaten an Ignite kill, so the lane is a survival race to your first item and level 6.

theirWindow.what: Disengage before he reaches 5 bleed stacks — his empowered W auto plus stacked passive true damage can burst you down with Ignite up. Only poke with Q (Lunge) from max range and break the trade in the wave, not in an extended 1v1.

yourWindow.when: Level 6+, he commits E or R
yourWindow.what: Hold W (Riposte) specifically for his E (Apprehend) pull or R (Noxian Guillotine) cast — parrying either negates his entire kill threat and stuns him for a free follow-up with your empowered autos.

start.why: Sustains through his early auto-poke and passive bleed ticks so you keep HP% and survive to level 6 without conceding the lane.

boots.why: Flat armor and auto-attack damage reduction blunt his AA-reliant trade pattern and Hemorrhage stacking speed.

core.why: Attack speed feeds your Q (Lunge) cooldown resets so you out-trade his slower attack cadence once you're allowed to fight.
Converts his max-stack Hemorrhage true damage and ult execute into damage-over-time you heal back or disengage from.
Armor shred and a slow keep him locked inside your empowered auto range where his lack of mobility punishes him.

situational.when: he's threatening to all-in you every wave and you need a safety net for a misplayed Riposte
he's snowballed and his auto-attack plus bleed burst is deleting you before your own damage lands
their team stacks hard CC beyond just Darius's kit

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks over extended trades and skirmishes, giving you the sustain and damage ramp to win prolonged fights once Riposte has opened the window.

summoners.why: Teleport resets you after early losses and keeps your item/level timings intact; Flash is your out when he lands E (Apprehend) or all-ins before your Riposte has value.

playing.title: Bank Riposte for his engage
playing.detail: Never spend W (Riposte) on a random auto — save it for E (Apprehend) or R (Noxian Guillotine), the only two abilities that actually threaten you.

playing.title: Deny stacks pre-6
playing.detail: Break off trades before Hemorrhage hits 5 stacks; a maxed stack plus his empowered W auto is where his all-in becomes lethal with Ignite.

playing.title: Freeze near your tower levels 3-5
playing.detail: His only gap closer is E (Apprehend); freezing outside its range removes his ability to engage without walking into your tower.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed E
playing.detail: If E (Apprehend) misses, he has no mobility left — this is your best window to all-in with Q (Lunge) resets and empowered autos.

playing.title: Track his ult reset range
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine refreshes its cooldown on a kill, so don't assume he's out of ult just because he used it on an earlier target.

playing.title: Fight around your vitals reveal
playing.detail: Use R (Grand Challenge) to relocate fights toward your revealed vitals, maximizing true damage procs and the movement zone against his lack of mobility.

playing.title: Build through his true damage
playing.detail: Death's Dance turns his passive and ult burst into delayed damage you can outheal or simply walk away from.

brief.patchCaveat: Item and rune names reflect the standard 16.x-era Fiora build (Kraken Slayer into Death's Dance, Conqueror keystone); verify exact numbers on Hemorrhage stacks and Riposte's parry window in-client since these shift patch to patch.
